card.title: CUI 2.0 design baseline

card.source: Source: tokens.less → build-css.mjs → tokens.css. Font tokens are in the specimen below. After changing a token run pnpm design:css — this page needs no edits.
card.sectionPairs: Key pairings (foreground on background · computed live)

card.typographyNote: Per-language stacks are mandatory: Traditional Chinese must not fall back to Simplified glyphs, and Japanese must not fall back to Chinese glyph forms.

redlines: Brand has two tiers: solid (--brand + white text) only for primary buttons/badges (max 2 per view); soft (--brand-soft + brand text) for selection, bubbles and avatars.
Never mix the amber tiers: --warm pairs with --warm-contrast; --warm-soft pairs with --warm-text.
In dark mode, brand text/outlines on soft fills must use --brand-lift.
All four interaction states (default/hover/active/disabled); keyboard focus must stay visible (--focus-ring).
--brand-display is fill-only: never put text or icons on it.
Success is soft fill + icon only; never a large solid fill.
Use --border-default/--border-control for controls; --border-subtle is decorative only.
No hardcoded colours in less/tsx (system colours excepted); always spell out token and class names.

f.title: Foundations · Spacing · Radius · Elevation · Motion · Border
f.subtitle: The P0 gaps: the baseline every page shares. Light on the left, dark on the right; values are read from tokens.css live.
f.source: Single source: tokens.less to build-css.mjs to tokens.css. Every value and colour on this page is read live; nothing is hardcoded.
f.langnote: Copy follows the language switch; values and colours do not.

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.note: A pure base-4 scale (4/8/12/16/24/32/48) with **no finer steps**: fewer choices means a steadier rhythm and removes the "is it 4 or 6" coin flip. No magic numbers; larger steps go further out.
spacing.example: Example: card padding 16, title to body 8, gap between buttons 12

radius.title: Radius
radius.note: Four steps: the larger the element, the larger the radius.

elevation.title: Elevation and shadow
elevation.note: A level is defined by shadow plus z-index; the scrim belongs to L3 only.
elevation.note2: In dark mode a shadow on a dark background is invisible, so levels are carried by tonal surfaces (--elevation-surface-1/2/3) plus a 1px warm white inner highlight; light mode still uses shadows.
elevation.stickyHint: While scrolling, the header stays at the top (z 100) and gains a shadow, which is the elevation behaviour of sticky. At rest it is just a normal title.

motion.title: Motion
motion.note: Duration by distance and importance; ease in with decelerate, out with accelerate.
motion.r1: Animate: panel open/close, dropdowns, press feedback, loading, streaming output, state changes.
motion.r2: Do not animate: scroll-follow, text reflow, frequent repeated micro-interactions.
motion.r3: Animate transform and opacity only (never width, height, top or left).
motion.r4: Reduced motion: when the system asks for less motion every duration collapses to zero inside tokens.less, so components need no special case.
motion.reducedOn: System preference: reduce motion - active (durations are zero)
motion.scenes: Common scenes (try them directly, or press play)
motion.ovNote: The same component, with .motion-quiet or .motion-rich on a container, changes intensity for that subtree only. The system reduce-motion flag is a master switch no local class can beat.

border.title: Border (with the WCAG 1.4.11 decision)
border.note: The field fill is only 1.05:1 from the content background, so the border is the only thing identifying an input, and 1.4.11 asks for 3:1.
border.d1: Keep the light border by default, for looks;
border.d2: Ship --border-control-strong and --border-hover-strong for the compliant look;
border.d3: When the system asks for more contrast, a media query in tokens.less switches automatically (verified in both themes).
border.deviation: This is a deliberate deviation: the default does not literally meet 1.4.11. If strict conformance is needed, point --border-control at the strong value - a one line change.

grid.title: Three columns (navigation | content | side)
grid.note: The main structure is three **vertical** columns on a grid, not horizontal bands. Give way order: the **side column shrinks first, then loses its track, and only then may the centre fall below its minimum**; the **navigation never concedes width**. Screen compatibility comes from **a default width per view type plus viewport driven collapse**, not from giving different screens different window sizes.
grid.contractTitle: Column contract (drag the sliders to see clamping)
grid.navCollapsedNote: collapse: client 0 (nav stays in the top left corner), web 56 rail
grid.centerMax: the remainder (inner text has its own readable cap)
grid.screenTitle: Screen compatibility (4K and 1080p share one set)
grid.s1: Thresholds are judged in **viewport CSS px**, which already include system scaling: 4K at 200% is about 1920 CSS px, the same as a 1080p display, so one set of rules reads correctly on both.
grid.s2: Column widths use **a default per view type** (reading 400, tool 600, task 640, wide 840) and are then held by **total width minus navigation, content minimum and handle**, so they grow on large displays and shrink on small ones.
grid.s3: The window only carries a default and a minimum (and remembers the last size). When height runs short the secondary toolbar goes and the **footer stays**.
grid.demo: Three column demo (drag the viewport, drag the columns, toggle)
grid.orderTitle: Give way order (the most expensive goes first)
grid.o1: The side column **shrinks first**, clamped between 300 and whatever space is actually left.
grid.o2: The side column then **loses its track entirely**: below 300 of remaining space it is simply not opened rather than squeezed.
grid.o3: **Only then may the centre drop below its minimum** of 400, and only once that track is gone.
grid.o4: The **navigation never concedes width**: below 1024 viewport it auto collapses to a 56px icon rail, and a manual expand **overlays** the centre instead of squeezing it.
grid.o5: In height: the secondary toolbar goes first and the **footer is kept to the very end**.
grid.navTitle: The three ways the navigation collapses (client and web)
grid.nr1a: Client or wide web (1024 and up)
grid.nr1b: **Collapses to 0**: the navigation area disappears and the content runs from the very left edge; the **traffic lights and the toggle do not move**, landing on top of the content, whose top row makes room with a left inset
grid.nr1c: Client: the top left corner beside the traffic lights, and it does not move
grid.nr1d: Persisted preference plus a transient flag (two levels)
grid.nr2b: **Keeps a 56px icon rail**, since a browser has no title bar to host the icons
grid.nr2c: Web has no traffic lights, so the entry point sits in the **top of the rail**
grid.nr2d: Same; a narrow expand never writes back to the preference
grid.nr3b: Drawer: floats over content with a scrim
grid.nr3c: Web drawer: a **hamburger in the content top row**
grid.nr3d: Transient (Esc or the scrim closes it)
grid.railNote: There is **no title bar**: three vertical columns, each with its own top row. Only the traffic lights and the toggle float in the top left corner, and they never move
grid.sideMaxFormula: **total width - (navigation + centre minimum + handle)**: drag freely up to that limit, no hard coded ratio
grid.sideHint: Drag the right edge of the content to resize the side column

ic.title: Icons and brand
ic.sub: Brand mark plus icon usage rules. The icons come from **lucide**: 24 grid, 2 stroke, ISC.
ic.brandNote: The mark answers "who is this"; interface icons answer "what can I do here". The two are **never mixed**.
ic.brandRule: **Use it whole**: no strokes, no rotation, no recolouring, no effects; clear space at least 25% of its height; 16px minimum
ic.uiRole: Meaning: what can I do here
ic.uiRule: **currentColor only**; 2 stroke on the 24 grid; nothing hand drawn, never mixing filled and linear
ic.d3: No colours beyond the brand colour
ic.d4: Never use the mark as an interface icon
ic.setNote: Interface icons come from **lucide** (24 grid, ISC). Our own marks are drawn by us and belong to the same family as the third party brands: `brand-yao-agents` and `brand-yao` (the taiji), listed first.
ic.spGridV: **24 x 24** (lucide rule; strokes stay at least 1px from the edge)
ic.spStrokeV: **2** (lucide rule, on the 24 grid). Scaled down for 14 and 16px it thins proportionally; if a size looks too thin, take that size to 2.25 as a whole
ic.spFillV: `fill: none`; solid shapes only where a dot genuinely needs it
ic.spColorV: `stroke: currentColor`, one colour source per icon
ic.spSizeV: Display sizes **14 / 16 / 20 / 24** (16 by default); the artwork itself is one 24 grid set
ic.galleryTitle: The full gallery (68, click one to copy our name for it)
ic.search: Search i-xxx, try file or plus
ic.specNote: Take from **lucide** by default. Only these five cases are drawn by us, and they still go on the **24 grid with a 2 stroke** so mixed icons stay consistent.
ic.r1: **Look first**: when you need an icon, find the closest meaning in lucide and use it. Do not draw a new one.
ic.r2: **Names stay ours**: `i-<domain>-<name>`, mapped one to one with the lucide name in `icons/manifest.json`.
ic.r3: **Only five cases are hand drawn**: the brand mark, coloured file type badges, meanings lucide lacks, state or process artwork, and simplified 14px variants.
ic.r4: **Hand drawn still means the same grid**: 24 x 24, 2 stroke, round caps and joins.
ic.r5: **Never change one stroke**: one source for the whole set; adjust a size step as a whole.
ic.a1: **Decorative** (text beside it): `aria-hidden="true"` with no accessible name.
ic.a2: **Meaningful**: `role="img"` and a `title`, or better, visually hidden text.
ic.a3: **Hit area**: a 16 icon still needs a target of at least 24, ideally 32.
ic.a4: **Never carry state by icon alone**: state is icon plus text plus colour.
ic.n2: Add it to `icons/manifest.json` (the lucide name for theirs, or `icons/own-sprite.svg` for ours) and run `build-icons.mjs` to re-inline.
ic.n3: Check it reads at **14px**; if not, draw a simplified version on the 24 grid.
ic.n4: Run the checks, `check-i18n` and `check-readme-values`, and confirm the page has no hard coded colour and no 16 grid leftovers.
ic.spCornerV: **2px** for elements 8px or larger, **1px** below that, about **2.41px** on diagonal right angles
ic.spGapV: At least **2px** between distinct elements (lucide rule)
ic.ruleTitle: Hand drawing rules (adopting the lucide spec)
ic.ruleNote: Only five cases are drawn by us, but the **geometry has to come from the same source as lucide** or mixed icons look wrong. These are the lucide **must** rules and we adopt them as they are; anything we break has to be **declared as an exception on this page**, which is what lucide itself requires of a must rule.
ic.rv1: **24 x 24** square, strokes at least **1px** from the edge
ic.rv2: **2px**, and **centred on the path** rather than inset
ic.rv3: **Round** caps on open paths and **round** corners everywhere
ic.rv4: At least **2px** between distinct elements and for inner gaps
ic.rv5: **2px** on elements 8px or larger, **1px** below that, about **2.41px** on diagonals
ic.rv6: Matches `circle` and `square`; **asymmetric icons may sit slightly off centre** so they look centred
ic.rs1: Detail density matches other icons; anything recognition does not need is **left out**.
ic.rs2: Smooth curves with no abrupt changes; prefer **arcs and quadratic curves**.
ic.rs3: Coordinates sit on the **pixel grid** where possible, but **visual quality wins**.
ic.rs4: Variants keep the base geometry, placement and orientation.
ic.rs5: Shared parts across related icons use **consistent** geometry, size and placement.
ic.rs6: When two should rules conflict, pick the one that is **clearer** and closer to the set.
ic.rx1: **Display steps 14 / 16 / 20 / 24**: lucide only designs for 24 and says nothing about small displays, so we declare **2.25 stroke across the 16px step** (about 1.5 visually), and a simplified variant at 14 where needed, still drawn on the **24 grid with a 2 stroke**.
ic.rx2: **Naming** stays ours, `i-<domain>-<name>`, mapped to lucide names in `icons/manifest.json`.
ic.rx3: **Hand drawing** is limited to the five cases above; everything else comes from lucide.
ic.brandsetNote: Model and vendor logos are each brand’s **official artwork**: an **official colour** variant, which trademark rules say must not be recoloured, and a **mono** one. **Official colours are the only place on this site allowed to use a colour that is not one of our tokens**; on a dark surface switch to mono. The logos are trademarks of their owners and identify the corresponding models or services. **A brand mark is identity, not an interface icon**, so the size defaults to **24** here (interface icons default to 16) and can be switched to 14, 16, 20 or 24. **General brands come in on demand**: for a non AI brand such as WeChat, Slack or Notion, `vendor-simple.mjs` converts that one brand.
ic.brandSearch: Search brands, try deepseek or openai
ic.coverBrandNote: {own} drawn by us (`brand-yao-agents` and `brand-yao`) plus {third} third party (`brand-*`, kept in separate sprites and referenced externally)

df.title: Data format · four languages
df.subtitle: Every value on this page is computed by the browser through **Intl at runtime**, not typed in. That makes it the **check** for the sample table in `plan/19-data-format.md` §3.4. Switch language to see the same data written the way each one does it.
df.s1hint: One instant rendered per language with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; relative time uses fixed sample intervals (`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`).
df.s2hint: Thresholds in `19` §3.1: just now → minutes → hours → days → month and day → year, month and day.
df.s3hint: One timestamp in four zones; the stored form carries the offset and the IANA zone in brackets (`19` §2).
df.s4hint: Grouping · compact · file size (binary, one decimal) · currency (each keeps its own decimals) · lists and ranges. **Technical identifiers stay Latin and left to right**.
df.s5hint: The same words through `Intl.Collator`; identifiers and paths are not localised and sort by code point (`19` §3.6).
df.s6hint: Directional icons mirrored · bidi isolation · visual regression — rules in `19` §4, demonstration in `css-logical.html`.
df.rtlMirrorValue: i-left · i-right · i-collapse · i-expand · i-act-undo · i-act-redo
df.rtlBidiValue: dir="auto" (user input / file names) · dir="ltr" + isolate (code / paths / identifiers)
